exposure: Inflammatory markers (white blood cell count slope)
outcome: Acquired infection during neonatal extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
cohort: This study included 160 neonatal patients under 30 days old who received extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support in a neonatal intensive care unit from 2003 to April 2016.
finding: Lower birth weight, vaginal birth, longer duration of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and a positive trend in white blood cell count 72 hours prior to infection were identified as factors increasing the risk of acquired infection in neonatal patients on ECMO.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was found to be more frequent in neonatal patients who developed confirmed infections during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support.
birth_weight: Lower birth weight was a risk factor for infection, but specific weights for the cohort were not mentioned.
